Bachelor’s thesis · Acoustic anomaly detection

Valve condition monitoring

Learning from sound to investigate valve anomalies when operating conditions and data distributions change.

The problem

Condition monitoring systems need to recognize anomalous behavior even when the data differ from the conditions seen during development. My bachelor’s thesis investigated acoustic anomaly detection for valves under domain shift.

What I built

I developed an audio-processing and anomaly-detection pipeline, transformed signals into frequency-domain and spectrogram representations, and used MobileFaceNet with sub-cluster AdaCos for learned representations. I investigated outlier exposure under domain shift.

Reported results

81.38% AUC · 72.29% partial AUC

Reported thesis evaluation results under domain shift. These are evaluation metrics, not classification accuracy.

The dataset split, partial-AUC operating range, and baseline comparison are not documented on this page; the figures should be read within the thesis evaluation context.
